headline: A new study found public performance evidence for fewer than half of the AI pathology and blood-cell diagnostic tools that regulators have cleared.
score_reason: Useful transparency finding, but it measures what is publicly findable rather than whether devices work; no change to score.
importance_line: Laboratories and hospital buyers, and ultimately patients, cannot easily compare cleared pathology AI tools, though the study does not show any tool is unsafe.
source: Streamline Feed, citing the npj Digital Medicine study and ThePrint
summary: Streamline Feed reports on a study in npj Digital Medicine, published 5 Oct 2026, which found public performance evidence for 30 of 77 CE-marked or FDA-authorized AI diagnostic tools in digital pathology and blood-cell analysis and none for the other 47. The researchers stress this shows what could be found publicly, not that the other devices were never validated.
notes: Credit goes to the outlet we read; it names the study and ThePrint.
